verdict.rationale: The only on-topic first-party evidence is a docs page titled "Slack charts, tables, and approvals." It suggests OpenClaw can surface approval prompts in chat, but says nothing about what they gate or how they work. Skill gating/allowlists (docs-116) govern skill loading, not shell commands, and sandboxing reduces blast radius rather than requiring approval, so neither counts here. A community comment that the default is full access is general criticism, not a concrete counter-example to approvals existing. missing for 10: documented command/exec allowlists, approval-prompt mechanics for dangerous actions, opt-in per-action elevated modes, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a self-hoster, dangerous actions require my explicit approval — command allowlists, approval prompts, and elevated modes that are opt-in per action
